pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-NMDA Receptor (NMDAR) Encephalitis THE SMOKING GUN: A pelvic transvaginal ultrasound revealing an unsuspected mature cystic ovarian teratoma containing ectopic neural tissue. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: The ectopic neural tissue within the ovarian teratoma expresses GluN1 subunits of the NMDA receptor, which are recognized as foreign antigens by the host immune system. This triggers the generation of autoantibodies (specifically IgG antibodies directed against the GluN1/NR1 subunit of the NMDA receptor). These antibodies cross the blood-brain barrier and bind to NMDA receptors on postsynaptic neuronal membranes, leading to cross-linking, antibody-mediated receptor internalization, and a profound reduction in NMDA receptor density. This results in the disruption of GABAergic interneuron regulation, causing massive frontostriatal and limbic disinhibition that clinically manifests as psychiatric symptoms, seizures, involuntary dyskinesias, and life-threatening autonomic instability. Prompt surgical resection of the teratoma and immunotherapy (corticosteroids, IVIG, or plasmapheresis) are curative.
